title: Access to guns a factor in fatal standoff, inquiry told
article: LONDON (CP) -- A flimsy plywood cabinet where a gunman got his arsenal the day he shot at his mother and a friend should never have been approved by police, a firearms official told a coroner's jury Tuesday.
On the last day of testimony in the inquest into _David_ _Melzer_'s shooting death, Det. Sgt. Lynn Pretty said the gun vault in the _Melzer_ home didn't meet accepted standards.
"If I had gone to Mr. _Melzer_'s home I wouldn't have approved that gun vault," she said.
The 33-year-old man was killed by police June 2, 2000, after an 11-hour standoff and shootout at his parents' home.
Pretty also said the man's father, John _Melzer_, should have had to move his guns out of the house when police learned his son was banned from guns.
A judge imposed the ban in 1996 following a 6 1/2-hour standoff in 1995 with Stratford police.
